title: China Is Building Its Way Around Europe’s EV Tariffs
gist: Aaron Glasserman and Jessie Jiexi Lin argue that Chinese EV competitiveness increasingly stems not just from subsidies but from a coordinated overseas industrial policy in which SOE-built infrastructure and resource access in places like Morocco become platforms for private Chinese battery and component makers. If Chinese firms complete EV assembly and supply-chain integration in Morocco, 'Made in Morocco' cars could enter the EU duty-free, cutting the tariff hit from up to 45 percent to zero and blunting Brussels' trade defenses.
